paragraphs: Hyman places Rabbah bar Itai in Rav’s time and refers to his entry on Rava bar Itai. For Sotah 30a he also proposes “Rabbah bar Itai said in the name of Rabbah,” adding that this requires further investigation.

notes.text: The supplied reading ends with Rabbah, but the consulted Sotah paragraph has Rabbah ben Isi reporting Rav. Hyman marks his proposed Itai reading as requiring further investigation. The opening relative clause may continue preceding text, which is not adopted as an established identification here.

The proposed Sotah reading is explicitly Hyman’s and retains his וצ״ע, “requires further investigation.” The recorded comparison has Rabbah ben Isi reporting Rav, against the supplied Itai/Rabbah wording. The opening relative clause may continue prior text, but that incomplete context and a separate uninspected Keritot search result do not establish an identity or support a new Sotah emendation.

In Hyman’s print (vol. III, p. 1071), the preceding notice about Rabbah bar Isi ends “and perhaps he is,” immediately before the heading Rabbah bar Itai. In the consulted Sotah 30a, Rav Asi reports Rav’s teaching, with Rabbah ben Isi named as the alternate reporter. Hyman’s cross-entry (p. 1058) gives “Rava (or Rabbah) bar Itai.” The consulted Shevuot 37a and Bava Metzia 14a read Rava, and the Hebrew of Keritot 24a reads Rabbah where the English has Rava. The identification and the proposed reading in Sotah remain tentative.
